findings.rationale: SC's observed outcome prevalence is far above what its features imply: calibration-in-the-large is strongly negative (z=-7.7), ECE is high (z=+5.8) and prevalence is elevated (z=+4.6), while local AUC is normal (0.819, pooled 0.819), which rules out label_noise. Per-round drift output shows prevalence about 0.2-0.4 with negative CITL from round 3 onward and no feature drift (shift_sd near 0 in most rounds), so the shift is on the label side and present from the start. Its O/E ratios are elevated across Sex and AgeGroup/Income subgroups, consistent with inflated positives. Its update norm is also anomalous (median norm ratio 3.1, z=+6.4), which fits a client whose labels disagree with its features rather than a poisoning attack, since its local performance is abnormal.

CA's observed prevalence is elevated relative to its features: CITL is strongly negative (z=-6.1), ECE is high (z=+3.3), and the observed/expected ratio is high in the Sex=1 subgroup (1.66, z=+7.1). Local AUC is high (0.846), so this is not label noise, and the subgroup pattern is over-recording of positives, not under-diagnosis. Per-round prevalence is elevated (about 0.2-0.29 vs pooled 0.14) from round 1. Its updates are also anomalous (median norm ratio 2.28, mean cosine 0.13), consistent with the label mismatch. Evidence is from several tools but CA's per-round CITL is noisier than SC's, so confidence is moderate.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of updates, performance, drift, features and subgroup outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed per-round drift for four candidates. Two clients show consistent evidence of prevalence shift from round 1: SC (strong: CITL z=-7.7, prevalence z=+4.6, normal AUC, anomalous update norm) and CA (moderate: CITL z=-6.1, elevated Sex=1 O/E, anomalous update norm, normal-high AUC). No feature drift, missing-value sentinel, poisoning, free-rider or explanation-instability signal was consistent across tools. Other leads (AK's Sex=1 O/E and drift, SD's late drift, VT's CITL, several small-client subgroup and feature outliers) stayed below the evidence threshold (|z| about 6 or a second independent confirmation) and were not reported. The full 20 epsilon was spent.
